newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross suspends work in Rwanda after killings.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross suspends work in Rwanda after killings.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross said on Wednesday that it was freezing its work in Rwanda for 10 days and pulling non-essential staff out of the country following Tuesday's killing of five U.N. employees.

The Geneva-based ICRC's spokeswoman Amanda Williamson said all ICRC operations in the tiny central African country, which mainly involve monitoring of prisoners and tracing of lost children, had been suspended for the next 10 days.
Gunmen killed four U.N. human rights monitors in an ambush near the southwestern town of Cyangugu in southwestern Rwanda on Tuesday. Their Rwandan driver was also wounded and later died.
The bodies of British and Cambodian monitors, 36-year-old Graham Turnbull of York, England, and 34-year-old Saspra Chim Chan of Cambodia, were flown to Nairobi after a Kigali memorial service.
Two Rwandan monitors were killed with them on a visit in a marked U.N. vehicle to Karengera commune in the southwest, bordering on Zaire.
"This period will enable the ICRC to analyse the situation, considering that six expatriates were killed in Rwanda these last three weeks," said Williamson.

The ICRC, which looks after war victims, prisoners and civilians in conflict zones, lost nine expatriate staff members in brutal attacks in 1996. Six medical employees were killed in December in Chechnya and three Swiss delegates in Burundi.

There have been a total of eight attacks on expatriates in Rwanda in the last three weeks, including three Spanish aid workers killed by unidentified gunmen and a 61-year-old Canadian missionary slain by a lone gunman on Sunday.
The ICRC said a number of non-essential staff were being sent to Kenya's capital Nairobi and the remainider would be on stand-by in Rwanda, where the organisation has 120 delegates.
The United Nations said it pulled all staff out of western Rwanda after a meeting on Wednesday of heads of U.N. agencies in Kigali to discuss how to respond to the increasing violence.
